rows.claim: At a fixed eigenvalue spectrum, transient amplification is governed by non-normality: holding the spectral radius constant and raising non-normality makes the worst-case transient grow by orders of magnitude.
rows.evidence: 2026-06-10_cc_data.json experiment_A: spectral_radius fixed at 0.8500 across all 7 levels while sup_transient rises 0.850 -> 994964.141 as Henrici departure rises 0 -> 27.04
rows.scope: synthetic N=100 operator, real Schur basis, strictly block-upper non-normal perturbation, spectral radius target 0.85

rows.claim: The spectrum is held EXACTLY fixed, so the transient growth cannot be an artifact of a drifting spectrum.
rows.evidence: spectral_radius_invariance_max_abs_deviation = 0.0 (spectral radius held at 0.8500 across all non-normality levels; strictly block-upper perturbation preserves the diagonal Schur blocks exactly)
rows.scope: construction control across Experiment A; the naive strictly-upper perturbation that moved the spectrum was rejected

rows.claim: A pseudospectral measure (the Kreiss constant) is a near-sufficient statistic for transient amplification, vastly outperforming the eigenvalue spectral radius.
rows.evidence: experiment_B (16 operators varying both spectrum and non-normality): R^2 of log sup_transient on log Kreiss = 0.991; on log numerical radius = 0.825; on log departure = 0.727; on spectral radius = 0.091
rows.scope: synthetic N=80 pool over 4 spectra x 4 non-normality levels

rows.claim: The crude non-normality scalar (Henrici departure) is NOT the right yardstick; the correct object is pseudospectral (Kreiss constant), as PRO conceded mid-duel.
rows.evidence: R^2 on log departure (0.727) is well below R^2 on log Kreiss (0.991); the numerical radius (0.825) also beats the raw departure scalar
rows.scope: Experiment B predictor comparison; concession that sharpened the thesis to the mathematically correct measure

rows.claim: Non-normality alone governs MEMORY the way it governs transients: at an identical spectrum, the more non-normal operator stores systematically more.
rows.evidence: experiment_C at identical spectrum (radius 0.9): normal operator memory_capacity 33.82 (departure 0) vs non-normal delay-line chain memory_capacity 26.27 (departure 5.94) — the chain remembers LESS, not more
rows.scope: synthetic N=100, noisy linear reservoir, Ridge readout, noise 1e-2, single fixed input vector

rows.claim: The eigenvalue spectrum is not a sufficient statistic for memory either (two operators differ in memory at an identical spectrum).
rows.evidence: experiment_C: identical spectral radius 0.9 yields memory_capacity 33.82 vs 26.27 — the spectrum alone does not fix memory, but neither does a single non-normality scalar
rows.scope: synthetic identical-spectrum memory comparison; cuts against BOTH a pure-spectrum and a pure-non-normality-scalar account

rows.claim: Real sparse synaptic (biological) matrices live in this regime, so the result transfers to neural connectomes.
rows.evidence: not tested — all operators are controlled synthetic constructions in a real Schur basis with strictly block-upper perturbations; no biologically sampled sparse synaptic matrix was used
rows.scope: would require biologically sampled sparse ensembles with the spectrum strictly controlled; not run by either side
